.\docs\cosign-verify-attestation-discipline.md:252:- **Accept a valid Sigstore signature WITHOUT checking artifact digest + cert identity against expected upstream** (Pattern A fix-forward edit #7 per codex T1 #7 prescription) — refuted: Sigstore signatures only attest "this artifact was signed by this identity at this time"; they do NOT validate the artifact is FROM your expected upstream/repo/workflow. .claude\rules\citation-discipline.md:42:6. **TIER-1-NAMED-AUTHOR-QUOTE class for inherited patterns** — when a SOTA pattern is derived from a named author's published work (book / peer-reviewed paper / conference talk), cite verbatim-quote + author-name + publication inline. The named-author cite is TIER-1 primary-source for the PATTERN (not the implementing repo); use alongside repo file:line cites for full provenance. Exemplar: `Z:/repos/deps/mattpocock/skills/README.md` (48,857★, MIT, [VERIFIED 2026-04-30 PM via curl raw GitHub]) quotes Pragmatic Programmer (Thomas & Hunt) for "rate of feedback is your speed limit" (failure-mode #3 framing), Domain-Driven-Design (Eric Evans) for ubiquitous-language pattern (#2 framing), and Extreme Programming Explained (Kent Beck) for "invest in design every day" (#4 framing). Per `.claude/projects/Z--claude-sota-installed/memory/reference_mattpocock_skills_pattern_extract_2026_04_30.md` for the full mining trace + adoption-candidate ranking. **TIER-1-NAMED-AUTHOR-QUOTE PROVISIONAL-EXCEPTION** *(round-3 framing per T3 round-2 conf=0.88 ESCALATING finding on commit `d4df352`; supersedes round-1 "full cardinal-rule-1 satisfaction" framing — physical-only sources do NOT fully satisfy committed-tree inspectability)*: physical-only printed-book/journal/conference-publication primary anchor (ISBN + page + verbatim-quote) is a PROVISIONAL-EXCEPTION to cardinal-rule-1 (CLAUDE.md L7), NOT full satisfaction. Cite class downgraded to TIER-1-NAMED-AUTHOR-QUOTE-PROVISIONAL with REQUIRED metadata: (a) ISBN/DOI + page + verbatim-quote inline; (b) verifier-identity disclosure (who-verified-when, e.g., `[VERIFIED 2026-05-04 by orchestrator against book Tip #15 verbatim text]`); (c) explicit `non-automatable: true` marker so review hooks know to defer to human sign-off; (d) **HARD-GATE ELIGIBILITY TEST** *(Round-3 amendment a per T3 R3 NEEDS-ATTENTION conf=0.82 same-class finding on commit `1b87a6e`; supersedes round-2 "MUST prefer" soft preference framing — preference is not gateable; eligibility is)*: PROVISIONAL admission is admissible ONLY when DOI landing page + accessible PDF / publisher excerpt / archived scan (license-permitting) was SEARCHED AND UNAVAILABLE. The commit body MUST document the search (which DOI/publisher/archive was queried + return shape — e.g., "searched ACM DOI 10.1145/<doi> 2026-05-05 — paywall-only, no excerpt found; searched Internet Archive — no scan; searched publisher excerpt page — none"). Mere preference is INSUFFICIENT — if any auditable surrogate exists (DOI/PDF/excerpt/scan), use it as the normative source instead of the physical-only book cite. e.g., ACM DOI `https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/<doi>` for ACM papers IS auditable when paywall-free. Secondary aggregator URLs (Wikipedia, `https://pragprog.com/tips/`, `https://martinfowler.com/bliki/<topic>.html`, `c2.com/cgi/wiki`) are VERIFICATION PROXIES only — they help re-verify the primary quote without owning the book physically, but are NOT cited as normative source. **Independent named-reviewer sign-off mandate** *(Round-3 amendment b per T3 R3 NEEDS-ATTENTION conf=0.82 same-class finding on commit `1b87a6e`; supersedes round-2 "Lower-confidence reviewer-sign-off mandate" sole-orchestrator framing — sole-orchestrator verification is no longer admissible)*: rule edits citing TIER-1-NAMED-AUTHOR-QUOTE-PROVISIONAL MUST cite a SECOND verifier-identity BEYOND the orchestrator who replayed the verbatim quote against the source — commit body MUST embed BOTH verifier-identity-1 (the orchestrator, e.g., `[VERIFIED 2026-05-05 by orchestrator against book Tip #15 verbatim text]`) AND verifier-identity-2 (the independent named reviewer, e.g., `[VERIFIED 2026-05-05 by <human-name> against same book + same page + same quote]`) with explicit `[VERIFIED yyyy-mm-dd by <name> against <source>]` markers for each. .claude\rules\convergence-gate.md:21:A new pattern, repo, SDK, or external primitive is ADOPT-NOW only when CONVERGENCE evidence is present. .claude\rules\convergence-gate.md:23:This gate stacks ABOVE the `.claude/skills/sota-research/SKILL.md` 5-row LOAD-BEARING bar (LOCAL — sota-research skill present at `.claude/skills/sota-research/SKILL.md`). .claude\rules\convergence-gate.md:33:Any axis failing = REJECT-until-convergence. Verdict line must name the specific missing axis + the exact evidence that would satisfy it.
.claude\rules\convergence-gate.md:50:4. **If ANY axis fails**, write `REJECT-until-convergence` as the verdict, with a bullet list specifying exactly what evidence would close each missing axis.
.claude\rules\convergence-gate.md:51:5. **Only then** run the sota-research 5-row bar. The convergence gate is a precondition — passing it doesn't auto-ADOPT, but failing it auto-REJECTS.
.claude\rules\convergence-gate.md:117:No single tool is authoritative. Running any ONE of the above in isolation produces narrow-grep false-negatives (single-tool signal ≠ convergence). The convergence check requires ≥3 distinct tool-types returning compatible evidence — otherwise treat the finding as "one-tool signal," which is not convergence.

# Reference: TIER-2 `docs/v11-doctrine-evolution.md` §"NEW FM-CANDIDATE-21" (W152-F4 codification anchor)

When Anthropic CC `/loop` skill operates in cron-mode (CronCreate) OR dynamic-mode (ScheduleWakeup), the prompt body is **frozen at queue time** and re-entered at fire-time (CronCreate recurring; ScheduleWakeup one-shot queue-time-to-fire-time context-freeze). If doctrine evolution, ship, or refutation lands BETWEEN queue-time and fire-time, the firing executes against STALE prompt context — directives in the queued prompt that have since been superseded, shipped, or refuted will be re-executed as if still pending. `[INFERRED from official scheduled-tasks docs exposing CronCreate/CronList/CronDelete but no CronUpdate primitive]` — auto-update of in-flight queued prompts is not documented; recovery is operator-action `CronDelete + CronCreate` (cron-mode) OR operator-discipline STATE PROBE before executing stale wakeup (dynamic-mode).

This rule is the **operator-discipline PEER to `fm20-path-drift-cascade.md`** — both handle propagation-class failures. FM-20 covers cross-fire claim-cite-trail propagation (via synthesis-vs-brief hop); FM-21 covers scheduler-queued-prompt staleness (via tick/wake mechanism). Distinct mechanisms; both require verify-before-execute discipline.

## Sub-classes (a/b) — taxonomy

| Sub-class | Mechanism | Signature | Recovery |
|---|---|---|---|
| **a CronCreate freeze** (recurring) | `CronCreate({cron, prompt, recurring})` stores prompt verbatim; re-fires identically each tick until explicit CronDelete | Active cron loads stale prompt at every `*/N * * * *` boundary; `[INFERRED]` no CronUpdate primitive documented → must `CronDelete + CronCreate` to refresh | Operator-action `CronDelete <id> + CronCreate <same-cron-expr, v(N+1)-prompt>` at doctrine-evolution-ship boundary. Codify cron-prompt-update emit as MANDATORY ship-step in `audit-action-loop.md §Stage 4 Re-fire` Wire→Surface→Close discipline (defers to next compact + fresh `/loop` invocation if operator unavailable) |
| **b ScheduleWakeup freeze** (one-shot queue-time-to-fire-time context-freeze) | `ScheduleWakeup({delaySeconds, prompt, reason})` stores prompt verbatim; fires once at deadline OR on `<task-notification>` wake; one-shot semantics, not recurring | One-shot wakeup fires with stale prompt that references work already shipped/refuted between queue-time and fire-time | Operator-discipline at fire-time STATE PROBE BEFORE executing prompt body: classify each queued prompt clause as shipped/refuted/still-current. If shipped/refuted → omit next ScheduleWakeup (end loop per `/loop` STEP 5); if still applicable → run with fresh-context override; if partial → execute applicable clauses + document stale clauses |

## Sub-class detail (operator-runbook expansions)

### FM-21.a — CronCreate freeze (recurring)

CronCreate is the primary cron-mode `/loop` entry: prompt body captured at create time + replayed each tick. `[INFERRED from /scheduled-tasks docs]` no in-place prompt update mechanism documented (only CronCreate / CronList / CronDelete). Doctrine-evolution ships within an active cron arc will land at runtime BUT cron tick continues to load STALE v(N) prompt. Recovery is operator-side: at doctrine-evolution-ship boundary, emit a manifest entry queuing `CronDelete <job_id> + CronCreate <cron, v(N+1)-prompt>` for next operator interaction. Sister to `audit-action-loop.md §Stage 4 Re-fire` Wire→Surface→Close discipline.

### FM-21.b — ScheduleWakeup freeze (one-shot)

ScheduleWakeup is dynamic-mode `/loop` self-pacing: orchestrator arms one-shot wakeup with `prompt` body that re-enters skill at fire-time. Per Anthropic CC `/scheduled-tasks` docs the prompt is queued verbatim and fires once at deadline (or on `<task-notification>` wake). If state changes between queue-time and fire-time (ship lands, refutation surfaces, parallel session shifts HEAD), the firing executes against stale prompt body.

Empirical evidence W152-F7-followup: orchestrator armed ScheduleWakeup 270s with prompt body framing "Voice 2 sota-researcher in-flight; on Voice 2 return synthesize convergence + Pattern A apply STUDY-PILOT-NARROW path". Voice 2 returned mid-window with **DEFER** verdict refuting STUDY-PILOT recommendation; W152-F7 shipped DEFER at commit `d55071f` 2026-05-11 16:20:07 -0400 (git committer timestamp; orchestrator-armed wakeup pre-dated commit). ScheduleWakeup fired ~5min after commit with STALE STUDY-PILOT-NARROW framing. Recovery: STATE PROBE HEAD confirmed `d55071f` persisted → no-op execute, end loop per `/loop` dynamic-mode STEP 5.

## When this rule applies

ANY of these triggers fires this rule:

1. Doctrine evolution lands at runtime (v(N+1) ships) while active cron `c<id>` is still firing v(N) prompt body verbatim
2. ScheduleWakeup armed with prompt referencing in-flight subagent dispatch OR mid-arc state; state changes (ship lands, refutation surfaces, HEAD shifts) before deadline
3. `/loop` cron-mode `recurring: true` job continues to fire across n+1 doctrine-evolution boundaries without operator-side CronDelete + CronCreate refresh
4. Cross-session resume: `/loop` cron survives session-close (recurring tasks auto-expire after 7 days per `/scheduled-tasks` docs); next session boundary's doctrine-evolution lands without operator-side refresh

## How to apply (operator + orchestrator-side discipline; recovery actions are COMPOSABLE not mutually exclusive)

### Recovery action #1 — CronCreate doctrine-refresh (sub-class .a)

When v(N+1) doctrine evolution lands at runtime:
1. List active cron jobs via `CronList`
2. For each cron loading v(N) prompt: `CronDelete <job_id>` + `CronCreate <same-cron-expr, v(N+1)-prompt>`
3. Document the refresh in commit body + MEMORY entry per `audit-action-loop.md §Stage 4 Re-fire` discipline
4. If operator unavailable: queue the refresh as Forward Top-5 item; cron continues firing v(N) until operator returns

### Recovery action #2 — ScheduleWakeup STATE PROBE clause-level smoke sequence (sub-class .b)

When ScheduleWakeup fires, BEFORE executing prompt body run clause-level smoke sequence:
1. `git log -5 --oneline` — recent commits (catch shipped work referenced in queued prompt)
2. `git status --short` — working-tree drift (signal parallel session activity)
3. `rg -n "<exact commit hash>|<decision keyword>|<workflow term>"` across `docs/sota-installed-manifest.md` + `docs/install-provenance.md` + relevant rule target — verify each clause's current applicability
4. **Classify each queued prompt clause** as:
   - `shipped` → omit clause from execution; document stale-fire
   - `refuted` → omit clause; document refutation source (Voice N verdict, codex T1, parallel session catch)
   - `still-current` → execute with fresh-context override
   - `partial` → execute applicable sub-clauses + document stale sub-clauses
5. If ALL clauses shipped/refuted → end loop per `/loop` STEP 5 (omit next ScheduleWakeup)
6. If ANY clauses still-current → execute applicable + ScheduleWakeup next iteration with FRESH prompt body matching current state
7. NEVER re-execute stale prompt without clause-level state-probe override

### Recovery action #3 — Audit-action-loop compounding instrumentation (closure around #1+#2)

Per `audit-action-loop.md` 4-stage Wire/Surface/Close/Re-fire — instrumentation that closes #1 + partially closes #2:
1. **Wire**: doctrine-evolution-ship hooks emit `STALE_CRON_DETECTED` JSONL records when active cron loads v(N) post-v(N+1)-ship
2. **Surface**: SessionStart additionalContext lists drifted active crons WARN-only
3. **Close**: operator CronDelete + CronCreate refresh (recovery #1) OR stale-wakeup recognition (recovery #2)
4. **Re-fire**: next cron tick verifies fresh prompt loaded; next ScheduleWakeup verifies state-probe-applied

## Anti-patterns

- **Treat stale ScheduleWakeup fire as user-message** — refuted by `/loop` STEP 4 semantics: `<task-notification>` IS the user-role wake, but the body is the queued prompt, NOT user intent. ALWAYS state-probe before executing.
- **Re-execute stale cron prompt without doctrine-refresh-check** — refuted by W152-F4 codification: active cron `c8617c3f` continues firing v10 doctrine post-v11 ship; each tick costs ~30s + token burn re-loading stale prompt against fresh runtime state.
- **Conflate `/loop` cron-mode with `/schedule` cloud-mode** — `/schedule` is cloud-persistent + operator-refreshable via /schedule UI; `/loop` cron-mode is session-lifetime + requires CronDelete + CronCreate for refresh per `/scheduled-tasks` docs. Different recovery paths.
- **Skip STATE PROBE before executing stale-wakeup prompt** — refuted by W152-F7-followup evidence: would-have re-shipped STUDY-PILOT-NARROW path that V2 sota-researcher refuted via Probe 7.b 5-clause check; state probe HEAD `d55071f` persistence verified W152-F7 DEFER ship intact → no-op execute correctly.
- **Promote FM-21 candidate at n=1 without cycle-322 OR cycle-321 fast-path justification** — refuted by `codification-threshold.md`. n=1 within W152-F4 was correctly classified as CANDIDATE; n=2 same-wave cross-subclass + cycle-321 expected-savings fast-path is the legitimate promotion threshold.
- **Cross-session resume stale-prompt acceptance** (NEW v11.1 anti-pattern) — when `/loop` cron survives session-close and re-fires at start of next session, the prompt may carry directives from session N that are stale for session N+1 (HEAD shifted, doctrine evolved, parallel ships landed). Apply Recovery #2 STATE PROBE clause-level smoke sequence at session-resume boundary AND at first cron tick post-resume.
- **Multi-day operator drift on cron-prompt-refresh queue** (NEW v11.1 anti-pattern) — if Forward Top-5 contains "operator CronDelete + CronCreate v(N+1) refresh" but operator unavailable for multi-day window, cron continues firing v(N) prompt accumulating stale execution context. Cost compounds: ~30s × N ticks/day × M days. Recovery: re-evaluate priority OR codify v(N+1)-detection-mid-tick override in `/loop` skill body.
- **Treat "HEAD contains shipped commit" as sufficient state-probe** (NEW v11.1 anti-pattern) — queued prompts often carry MULTI-CLAUSE directives (e.g., "synthesize + ship + APPEND provenance + PREPEND MEMORY + next-action recommendation"). Single-commit HEAD verify only catches the FIRST clause; later clauses may still apply OR be stale independently. Recovery #2 clause-level smoke sequence required.

## Sub-class detail (operator-runbook expansions)

### FM-17.a — Wrapper-truncation
SendMessage re-emission typically succeeds because substantive reasoning is already done — gap was FINAL handoff, not analysis. Agent B Fire 35a precedent: SendMessage `ae1aaad7e9ce7ba40` recovered.

### FM-17.b — Pool-depletion 429
Pool-funneling per CLAUDE.local.md ENV (f) means simultaneous parallel agents drain Sonnet pool exactly when handoff fires. **For ADOPT-class verdicts**: lost adversarial-review surface BLOCKS the ship until either (a) reviewer re-dispatched and returns verdict, OR (b) explicitly equivalent cross-model review (codex T1 deep-review-exec) completes. **Mia pre-apply is a prescription-validity check ONLY** — does NOT satisfy or replace the adversarial-review gate for ADOPT-class verdicts (per T3 NEEDS-ATTENTION conf=0.88 iter-2 escalation on commit `2e7deae`). **STAND-IN-NOTICE mandate** (Wave 48 Agent A F-1 conf=0.91 on commit `5e0bf2b`): if orchestrator-side Mia substitutes for re-dispatch, commit body MUST include `gpt5-reviewer LOST (FM-17.b pool-depletion); adversarial-review surface substituted via orchestrator Mia pre-apply; cross-model gate NOT satisfied for this ship; T1 re-review queued.` per `cross-model-consensus.md §Env-funneled subagent stand-in disclosure mandate`. Disclosure alone does NOT satisfy the gate.

#### b.i + b.ii sub-promotion threshold
Codification unit is the **shared parent mechanism** (env-pin Sonnet wrapper-funneling per CLAUDE.local.md ENV (g)) — NOT individual b.i/b.ii timing signatures. n=4 same-arc 2026-05-06 satisfies cycle-322 promotion at parent-mechanism level. b.i/b.ii are observable timing-discriminator signatures, useful for operator triage. **Orchestrator-direct fallback constraints** (T3 NEEDS-ATTENTION conf=0.78 finding F-2 on commit `5e0bf2b`): when pivoting, (i) preserve read-only posture if original agent role was read-only; (ii) prefix work with STAND-IN-NOTICE per `cross-model-consensus.md` Option 2; (iii) require codex T2/T3 second-model review before shipping; (iv) emit `FM-17.b.{i,ii} pool-{pre-fire,mid-exec} fallback to orchestrator-direct; cross-model gate NOT satisfied; T1 re-review queued`. **Sister observation** (n=1 FORWARD-REF): worktree-cleanup-leak — agent-* worktrees remain LOCKED after Sonnet wrapper crash, bypassing auto-cleanup per `parallel-session-worktree-isolation.md`.

### FM-17.c — Codex execution wedge
**.c.i candidate root causes** (Wave 26 Agent A diagnosis): (1) cwd/slug-hash mismatch — companion `state.json` writes to `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}/state/<slug>-<sha256(cwd).slice(0,16)>/` per `state.mjs:8-52 @ HEAD 807e03ac`, dispatch-cwd may differ from probe-cwd (MOST CONSISTENT for Wave 25 task-mot7qnh5-azhcys); (2) spawn-before-write TOCTOU at `codex-companion.mjs:654-680`; (3) Windows ACL on `.codex/sessions`; (4) CODEX_HOME env drift; (5) PowerShell vs Bash subprocess handle inheritance. **.c.ii root cause**: `CertOpenCurrentUserStore` denied in worktree process even though `CODEX_HOME` auth files present. Per `codex-t1-fix-forward-pattern.md §Pattern B` HNF: examine bg job stderr/tee files for partial trace; if mineable, integrate as Sonnet stand-in BLOCKED-PROVISIONAL. **Wave 26 Lesson 2 correction**: foreground+tee fixes .c.i but NOT .c.ii; per `port-note-discipline.md §6` correction is FORWARD-ONLY.

### FM-17.d — BRIDGE-MODE wrapper stall
Sonnet wrapper's stream-watchdog 600s timeout is shorter than typical foreground `codex exec -p deep-review-exec` xhigh reasoning duration (empirical 5-15min per `cross-model-consensus.md §Profile selection rule`). Watchdog fires before codex emits next stream chunk; wrapper has no recovery primitive. **Cascade BLOCK gate (.d + .c.ii)** (Wave 48 Agent A F-3 conf=0.82): if foreground+tee from MAIN orchestrator session ALSO fails with cert-store ACL signature, STOP all retries; emit `VERDICT: BLOCK — BRIDGE-MODE and main-session foreground+tee both unavailable (FM-17.d + FM-17.c.ii cascade); cross-model gate suspended; no ship until Windows cert-store ACL remediated`. Pressure-driven shortcut to defer-queue WITHOUT BLOCK is anti-pattern. Sister to .c.i recovery (foreground+tee) and `cross-model-consensus.md §Env-funneled subagent stand-in disclosure mandate` STAND-IN-NOTICE — when .d fires and operator pivots to foreground+tee, verdict origin remains REAL GPT-5.5 (cross-model gate satisfied).

### FM-17.e — Autocompact-thrashing
CC-runtime autocompact mechanism: when single tool output exceeds context-window threshold, autocompact fires; if agent's brief re-issues same large-content tool call, post-compact context refills immediately and triggers autocompact again. After 3 consecutive thrash-cycles, CC-runtime self-aborts. Differs from .d in failure surface: .d is Sonnet-wrapper-watchdog (600s gap on codex-CLI stream); .e is CC-runtime-autocompact (context refilled 3 turns post-compact, 3 times). For LOST verdict: trace-mining is N/A (no partial output); HONEST-NON-FINDING per `synthesis-layer-verify.md §Reporting categories`. Same-fire n=2 in Wave 112 Ship A1 dispatch (Agents B `a9b7a29764e29782f` + C `a3c48b6aed8ece998` both BRIDGE-MODE codex-rescue with same multi-source ecosystem probe scope) — diagnostic discriminator vs .d is literal notification text ("stream watchdog" vs "Autocompact is thrashing"). Wave 165 P0-B Agent `a7c0d4332e285591b` (n=5 firm; 4-repo audit scope karpathy+pocock+awesome-claude-code+claude-skills under codex-rescue BRIDGE-MODE) replicates Wave 112 multi-source-probe failure shape — confirms Pattern: BRIDGE-MODE codex-rescue + multi-repo ecosystem probe scope → autocompact-thrash. Recovery applied per /goal P0: Path P codex exec foreground+tee dispatch (Agents C+D) bypassed FM-17.e successfully at trace level (substantive 30237 + 4333 line outputs) but produced Pattern B HNF on JSON-verdict emission — disposing 0.5 cross-model gate weight each per `cmc-verdict-shapes.md §Verdict report shape`.

### FM-17.f — 1M-context-entitlement billing-class blocker
Per `docs/fm17f-deep-dive-2026-05-09.md` Wave 119 deep-dive: parent session's `[1m]` context flag carries into subagent session-creation request INDEPENDENTLY of subagent frontmatter `model:` resolution per TIER-1-DIRECT `https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents §"Choose a model"` 4-step model-resolution order (env > per-invocation > frontmatter > main-conversation). With subagent frontmatter `model: sonnet`, resolved request becomes effective `sonnet[1m]` because parent's `[1m]` flag propagates to child session-creation. On plans where Sonnet 1M requires `/extra-usage` (per `https://code.claude.com/docs/en/model-config §"Extended context"`), request fails at billing-class entitlement check BEFORE any tool call or token consumption. Mechanism INFERRED from pre-fire 0-token observation — NOT TIER-1-verified architecture per codex T1 W119 NEEDS-REVISION conf=0.91 AXIS-2 correction at `.claude/state/codex_consult_w119_fm17f_path_d_setup_OUT.txt`. Path P proven E2E per fm17f-deep-dive §2; Path D activated ONLY for explicit fan-out Waves declaring 3-5 BRIDGE-MODE subagent dispatch as load-bearing per `advanced-agent-team-standing-directive.md` invariants. For LOST verdict when Path P/D unavailable: HONEST-NON-FINDING per `synthesis-layer-verify.md §Reporting categories`.

## When this rule applies

ANY of these triggers:
1. Subagent task-notification with `<status>completed</status>` + truncated `<result>` body
2. Subagent task-notification with `<result>...429...cooling down</result>` after substantive duration_ms
3. codex-rescue BRIDGE-MODE wrapper returns "task forwarded" but bg job verdict file never lands (FM-17.c.i companion-job state wedge)
4. Direct foreground `codex exec` reaches model/provider/session initialization, then fails with `failed to open current user certificate store` / `Access is denied` / `stream disconnected before completion` (FM-17.c.ii Windows cert-store ACL wedge — distinct from .i: no bg job involved, fires in codex CLI's own TLS-handshake)
5. Pre-fork dispatch attempt fails with API rate-limit BEFORE Agent tool returns agentId
6. BRIDGE-MODE GPT-5.5 subagent task-notification with `<status>failed</status>` + "stream watchdog" / "Agent stalled" / "INTERNAL_ERROR after N tool_uses" without 429 / cert-store / companion-bg-job signatures (FM-17.d wrapper-watchdog stall)
7. Subagent task-notification with `<status>completed</status>` + literal "Autocompact is thrashing: the context refilled to the limit within 3 turns of the previous compact, 3 times in a row" + minimal usage (typical 4 tool_uses / 146-164 tokens) + substantive duration_ms (~989-1180s) (FM-17.e CC-runtime autocompact-thrashing)
8. Subagent task-notification with `<status>failed</status>` + literal "API Error: Extra usage is required for 1M context · run /extra-usage to enable, or /model to switch to standard context" + pre-fire <2s wall-clock + 0 tool_uses + 0 tokens + parent session launched with `[1m]` flag (FM-17.f extended-context subagent pre-fire 1M-context-entitlement billing-class blocker)

## Anti-patterns

- **Silent re-dispatch to depleted pool**: refuted by §FM-17.b recovery — fleet probe FIRST per `parallel-agent-wave.md §CADP rule 5`; re-dispatching without status.py probe wastes another wall-clock window AND repeats the failure
- **Treat truncated `<result>` as honest-non-finding**: refuted by sub-class (a) recovery — substantive work happened; SendMessage re-emission typically succeeds; abandoning is wasted compute
- **Treat bg-job-no-verdict as agent-side bug**: refuted by sub-class (c) — usually orchestrator-side env / permissions / config drift. Distinguish at error-shape: missing job state file → FM-17.c.i (investigate cwd-slug-hash mismatch + companion `writeJobFile` TOCTOU + CODEX_HOME drift); transport/TLS-layer error like `failed to open current user certificate store` AFTER successful model-init → FM-17.c.ii (investigate Windows cert-store ACL on the codex exec process identity, not companion state). Treating .ii as a job-state issue produces wasted CODEX_HOME/sessions/ probes; treating .i as a cert-store issue produces wasted ACL probes
- **Bundle FM-17 recovery with FM-19 readonly-guard fix**: separate concerns — FM-19 ARTIFACT-INLINE mandate is the *prevention* (codified by `advanced-agent-team-standing-directive.md` invariant #5); FM-17 is the *post-hoc recovery* when prevention insufficient
- **Skip iter-close documentation of loss**: refuted by `audit-action-loop.md §Surface stage` — silent FM-17 losses accumulate as "compute spent without verdict landed"; track each loss in close-synthesis MD with sub-class label

- **Treat 600s stream-watchdog stall as agent-side stuck**: refuted by sub-class (d) recovery -- codex CLI subprocess was healthy; wrapper watchdog fired prematurely on xhigh reasoning chunks. Foreground+tee from main session bypasses; do NOT re-spawn subagent with same open-ended brief -- re-brief with per-call budget OR escalate to main-session dispatch

- **Treat autocompact-thrashing as agent-side stuck OR codex-CLI failure**: refuted by sub-class (e) — failure surface is CC-runtime autocompact mechanism, NOT codex-CLI subprocess (codex never invoked in .e-class fires per minimal 4-tool-uses signature). Re-dispatch with SAME brief that triggered .e is anti-pattern (will autocompact-thrash again). Brief MUST be tightened: substitute `Read` of large files with `mcp__plugin_context-mode_context-mode__ctx_execute_file`; substitute `WebFetch` with `mcp__plugin_context-mode_context-mode__ctx_fetch_and_index`; cap exa/perplexity searches with `head_limit`; bound Bash outputs with `head -N`. Sister to FM-17.d in recovery (foreground+tee from main session bypasses subagent context entirely) but distinct in failure surface (.d=Sonnet-wrapper-watchdog 600s; .e=CC-runtime-autocompact 3-cycle-thrash)

# TIER-3 local: this rule was promoted from `.claude/projects/Z--claude-sota-installed/memory/feedback_fm20_path_drift_cascade_n3_cross_arc_2026_05_05.md` (n=3 codification-anchor at write-time) to standalone rule at n=5 cumulative + n=4 same-arc 2026-05-05 per `codification-threshold.md` cycle-322 jurisdiction n≥3 self-observed promotion bar + memory file:83 explicit update trigger ("n=4+ same-arc would promote META-router to dedicated rule"). Recursive promotion-fire shape matches Wave 16 fire-7 mia-pre-apply.md + Wave 17 D1 fm19-readonly-guard-sidestep.md + Wave 24-D advanced-agent-team-standing-directive.md + Wave 34 fm17-subagent-fleet-depletion.md precedents.

When an agent (sota-researcher / architect / general-purpose / Explore / code-reviewer / debugger / codex T1) returns a ship-prescription containing claim X — OR when stale task-tracking text / prior memory snapshot / past-fire summary records claim X — and that claim becomes the source-of-truth for orchestrator-side synthesis → next fire's task brief → next agent's dispatch context, the wrong claim propagates 1-3 fires before runtime probe surfaces refutation. The recovery is decompose-by-sub-claim Mia probe at synthesis-vs-brief boundary, NOT only at apply boundary (which `mia-pre-apply.md` covers).

This rule is the **propagation-boundary peer to mia-pre-apply.md's apply-boundary discipline** — same shape (verify-before-trust) applied at different boundary points across multiple fires.

## The drift cascade structure

The drift cascade has 3 propagation hops:

```
[Agent A return / stale text] → Orchestrator synthesis → Task brief → Agent B dispatch → Mia probe at runtime → REFUTED
   (claim X)                       (verbatim cite)        (verbatim cite)   (assumes X)        (catches OVER)
```

Each hop preserves X verbatim because there's no cheap probe at the hop boundary; Mia is currently codified at the **apply boundary** (per `mia-pre-apply.md §How to apply`), not at every cite-propagation boundary. FM-20 codifies the synthesis-and-brief-composition boundaries explicitly.

## When this rule applies

ANY of these triggers fires this rule:

1. Agent return contains multi-clause prescription (3+ independent claims that could be sub-decomposed)
2. Orchestrator-side synthesis cites a prior agent verdict / memory file / task tracking text VERBATIM in next-fire brief
3. Next-fire brief carries claim X without explicit `[VERIFIED via <probe>]` marker per `cross-model-consensus.md §Evidence marker discipline` MUST-USE convention
4. Cross-fire propagation suspected: claim X originated 1-3 fires back; no runtime probe at any hop boundary

## How to apply (forward-only convention)

When an agent return contains multi-clause prescriptions:

1. **Decompose by sub-claim** — break the agent's "X+Y+Z" return into 3 independent claims; each gets its own probe shape per `synthesis-layer-verify.md §Subclaim-type discriminator` (UPSTREAM/OPERATIONAL/CATEGORY)
2. **Mia-probe each sub-claim INDEPENDENTLY at synthesis time** — do NOT cite X verbatim into the next-fire brief without runtime probe
3. **Cite the probe outcome verbatim in synthesis** — "Agent A claim X1: VERIFIED via `Grep`; X2: REFUTED via `Read file:line`; X3: PENDING-PROBE"
4. **Refuted sub-claims DROPPED from next-fire brief** — do not propagate
5. **At next-fire dispatch**: brief cites only verified sub-claims + explicit `[VERIFIED via <probe>]` markers per `cross-model-consensus.md §Evidence marker discipline` MUST-USE convention codified iter-107

## Recovery actions when FM-20 fires

When current-fire Mia probe surfaces propagated OVER from N-fires-back:

1. **DROP refuted sub-claim from current fire's apply scope**
2. **Document refutation in commit body** with `[VERIFIED via <probe>]` cite-trail
3. **Pivot ship to verified-surviving prescriptions** OR HONEST-NON-FINDING if all sub-claims refuted (per `synthesis-layer-verify.md §Reporting categories`)
4. **Trace cite-propagation backward** through prior synthesis docs to find the originating agent claim (helps ladder-tracking)
5. **Forward-only correction** per `port-note-discipline.md §6` — do NOT rewrite historical commit bodies; correct the LIVE state and codify forward

## Anti-patterns

- **Cite agent claim verbatim into next-fire brief without sub-claim Mia probe** — refuted by n=5 cumulative cross-arc evidence. Agent confidence ≥0.85 does NOT correlate with sub-claim accuracy. Each sub-claim needs its own probe.
- **Synthesize first, probe later** — refuted by Wave 19 fire-22 evidence: orchestrator-side synthesis-Mia caught D2 + C OVER claims AFTER agent return but BEFORE fire-23 dispatch (3-OVER catch documented at commit `d2a765e` body). The probe-at-synthesis catches before propagation hop 2; without it, the OVER reaches next agent's dispatch context.
- **Treat task-tracking text as authoritative for source-of-truth claims** — refuted by Wave 37 AGENTS.md catch. Task tracking text (e.g., "GAP CONFIRMED ~170 LOC draft ready" in task #512) records state AT WRITE-TIME; subsequent ship-completion commits close gaps but task text doesn't auto-update. Per `evidence-policy.md` Marker Decay corollary.
- **Treat HONEST-NON-FINDING as agent failure** — per `synthesis-layer-verify.md §Reporting categories` HNF distinction. An agent that probes its own claim and self-refutes (Agent A fire-22 ccusage self-catch; Agent A Wave 37 reverse-Mia AGENTS.md+context7) is the highest-quality return shape — preserve as evidence, do not re-spawn.
- **Skip the recursive-OVER probe at synthesis layer** — refuted by Wave 19 fire-22 close: synthesis-Mia caught 3 OVER claims that would have shipped if I'd cited Agent D2's "graphify NEW" verbatim into fire-23 brief. The probe budget is cheap (1-3s) vs revert cost (5-15 min).

# Parallel session worktree isolation — outer-layer Cherny pattern

## The rule

When TWO OR MORE `claude` CLI sessions operate concurrently against the same checkout, EACH session MUST start with `claude --worktree` (or `-w`) so each session gets its own isolated working tree under `.claude/worktrees/`. The launcher `tools/eee.ps1` forwards `--worktree`/`-w` per `tools/eee.ps1:--worktree forwarding block` symbol-anchor (per `port-note-discipline.md §2 Discipline 1`) (shipped via codex T1 NEEDS-REVISION conf=0.88 gap-resolution arc 2026-05-02 commit `f3c1e57`) — mandate is now hard MUST, no longer SHOULD-WHEN-AVAILABLE. Without this isolation, one session's `git rm` + `git add` + `git commit` sequence can interleave with another session's pending stage operations, producing audit-trail mismatches where commit content does not match commit message.

This rule applies to the OUTER (CLI launch) layer. The INNER (agent-spawn) layer is already covered: all 8 sss agents declare `isolation: worktree` per `^isolation:` grep across `.claude/agents/` [VERIFIED 2026-05-04 via Wave 18 architect audit grep returned 8/8]; symbol-anchor avoids stale-count drift per `port-note-discipline.md §1 Discipline 1`. Agent-level isolation handles `Agent()` tool spawns; outer-level isolation handles separate `claude` invocations.

## Why

Concrete failure instance, 2026-04-27 master timeline:

| Time | Session A | Session B (mine) | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 10:37 | Wrote `permission_request_auto_approve.py` + companion via Bash heredoc | — | files on disk |
| 10:38 | — | Codex T6 stop-gate caught HIGH-severity defect; executed REVERT-AND-REMOVE per closed-loop-recursive-narrowing.md Outcome B; `rm` files; `git rm` + `git add .gitignore` staged | files gone, deletions staged |
| 10:41 | — | Tried `git commit -m "fix(security): REVERT-AND-REMOVE..."`; landed as commit `5d22b16` | commit landed with INTENDED Session B content |
| 10:42 | Tried `git commit -m "feat(auto-proceed): full Cherny mode..."` | — | landed as commit `7067f0b` BUT bundled Session B's earlier staged deletions; commit MESSAGE = Session A intent, commit CONTENT = mostly Session B safety-revert |
| 10:43 | — | Truthful follow-up commit `00fdabf` documenting the race | clean state restored |

The shared working directory is the load-bearing race surface. `git add` and `git commit` are not atomic across sessions; they read the index at commit time, which can include changes another session staged 2 seconds earlier. Worktree isolation removes the shared surface entirely — each session has its own `.git/index`.

## How to apply

**At session start:**

```bash
# Wrong (parallel sessions same checkout)
claude                                    # session A
claude                                    # session B in another terminal — RACE RISK

# Right (each session in its own worktree)
claude --worktree                         # session A — auto-creates .claude/worktrees/<auto-name>/
claude --worktree feature-x               # session B — explicit branch name
```

**Mid-session (if you realize you should have started in a worktree):**
Ask Claude: "move this work to a worktree". CC will create one and migrate the in-flight changes via `git worktree add` per code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference §worktree.

**For agents (already shipped at sss):**
Frontmatter declaration `isolation: worktree` causes every Agent() spawn to operate in `.claude/worktrees/agent-<id>/`. Verify in your agent definition; all 8 sss agents already have this [VERIFIED 2026-05-04 via Wave 18 architect grep `^isolation:` across `.claude/agents/` returned 8/8].

**For automation scripts (sss.ps1 launcher):**
Shipped via `tools/eee.ps1` explicit `--worktree` / `-w` forwarding. Per codex T1 NEEDS-REVISION conf=0.88 verdict at `.claude/state/codex_consult_gap_resolution_2026_05_02_OUT.txt`. Cite: `Z:/repos/deps/claude-code-best-practice-shan/best-practice/claude-cli-startup-flags.md:125 @ f8468e871ed372f2807aa9d3ca7ca91eca7db422 [VERIFIED 2026-05-02 — refreshed from prior `41f503c9` per Ship 48 + linter sweep on canonical.md L8 + layered-gates-architecture.md L15-16; closes Wave 10 Agent B P3-2 partial-orphan]` + `https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tutorials` (Anthropic worktree pattern).

## Sub-classes (cumulative iter-99 codification — META-router enriched at `named-failure-modes.md` FM-02 row)

Per `named-failure-modes.md` FM-02 META-router row updated iter-99 commit `675aba9` to n=7 cumulative evidence + 5 numbered recovery patterns, the parallel-session race surface decomposes into 3 distinct sub-classes — all OWNED by this rule but with different observation surfaces and recovery patterns. The META-router carries the cite-anchored evidence ladder; this OWNER rule carries the mechanics.

### Sub-class (a) — T2-review contamination

**Signature**: codex T2 invocation reviews ALSO untracked/modified files from concurrent parallel `claude` session, causing T2 verdicts to flag contamination NOT authored by the current session [VERIFIED 2026-05-02 via iter-104 T2 state file Q5 contamination-check prompt + Q7 P1 staging/process blocker (commit `9a22d27` documents narrow `--only` exclusion); iter-105 T2 state file P1 staged-deletion contamination of `bundle6-skills-audit.md` (commit `011d885` documents resolution via narrow `&&` chain after parallel session shipped Ship 36)].

**Recovery** (per FM-02 META-router row #1 + #3 + cardinal-rule reporting): narrow `git add -- <my-file>` BEFORE T2 fires (row #1) + close via single-shell `git add -- <my-file> && git commit -o <my-file> -F <msg>` chain after the T2 check (row #3 atomic-batch per `audit-action-loop.md` step 4) + report contamination per cardinal-rule 7 (CLAUDE.md §Hard Rules, bullet "REPORT errors before routing around them") rather than silently filtering it.

### Sub-class (b) — Staging-index race

**Signature**: my staged files become unstaged or get parallel-session staging silently mixed into my `git diff --cached` between my `git add` and `git commit` [VERIFIED 2026-05-02 via iter-91 + iter-94 + iter-95 + iter-97 same-arc instances per `named-failure-modes.md:24` FM-02 row "n=5 same-arc 2026-05-02"].

**Recovery** (per FM-02 META-router row #2+#3): narrow `git commit --only -- <pathspec>` or short `git commit -o <pathspec>` form scopes commit to named paths regardless of broader index state — primary defense against staging-index race. Combined with single-shell-invocation `git add <file> && git commit -o <file> -F <msg>` chain per `audit-action-loop.md` step 4 atomic-batch.

### Sub-class (c) — COMMIT-LAYER ABSORPTION (NEW iter-98)

**Signature**: parallel session's `git commit -a` or expanded pathspec sweeps my modified-unstaged file into THEIR commit before I can complete my own T1+T2+commit cycle. Semantic ship lands but audit-trail attribution drifts [VERIFIED 2026-05-02 via iter-98 absorbed into Ship 29 commit `12e32ff`].

**Recovery** (per FM-02 META-router row #4): accept the absorption (do NOT rewrite history per `port-note-discipline.md §6` anti-pattern "Do not rewrite historical commit bodies"); document via supplementary memory + audit-trail correction in subsequent commit body when feasible.

### Long-term defense (per FM-02 META-router row #5)

Each session uses `claude --worktree` for full filesystem isolation (Layer 0 of `layered-gates-architecture.md` §3 worktree isolation prerequisite). Filesystem-level isolation prevents all 3 sub-classes structurally; the narrow-`--only` recovery patterns above are stop-gap defenses until full Layer-0 isolation is universal across operator launch paths.

## Mandatory mechanical collision-guard (Round-2 fix-forward per T3 round-1 NEEDS-ATTENTION)

### The mandate (narrow scope)

Every JSONL-emitting hook in `.claude/hooks/scripts/*.py` MUST do BOTH:

1. **Persist `agent_id` + `agent_type` when present in hook input** (per `audit-action-loop.md §Hook telemetry contract`). For main-session writes where `agent_id` is absent (None / null), persist `null` explicitly so consumers can distinguish "main session" from "absent attribution". This is **attribution**, NOT collision prevention.

2. **MANDATORY collision boundary** — pick ONE of:
   - **(a) Atomic temp-rename for FULL-FILE writes ONLY**: write to `<path>.tmp.<nanos>.<pid>`, then `os.replace` (cross-platform atomic on POSIX + Windows NTFS). Use ONLY for FULL-FILE write-once classes where last-writer-wins is acceptable (e.g., `codex_review_HEAD_<sha8>.txt` written once per commit, `codex_consult_<topic>_<pid>.txt` written once per consult). NEVER use this option for SHARED JSONL append targets — `os.replace` does atomic file-swap but does NOT merge concurrent appends, so two writers concurrently doing read-modify-replace can drop earlier records (lost-update race). For NO-CLOBBER first-write semantics, use `os.open(path, os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL | os.O_WRONLY)` for exclusive creation; fail closed (caller catches) if collision detected.
   - **(b) Filename-namespace**: include `<agent_id8>` or `<process_id>` in filename so concurrent writers cannot collide on the same path (e.g., `codex_review_HEAD_<sha8>_<agent_id8>.txt` or `codex_consult_<topic>_<pid>.txt`). Consumers must merge across the namespace if a unified view is needed.
   - **(c) Lockfile + O_CREAT|O_APPEND atomic-write for SHARED JSONL append**: open the JSONL log with `os.open(path, os.O_CREAT | os.O_APPEND | os.O_WRONLY, mode)` where `mode` defaults to `0o600` (owner-only — per Round-5b T3 round-3 NEEDS-ATTENTION conf=0.78 NEW-CLASS trust-boundary finding on commit `c2b5dee`: `0o644` was world-readable and leaked audit-trail content (agent prompts, PIDs, verdict cite paths, `agent_id` UUIDs, T1/T2/T3 verdict bodies) on multi-user hosts. Callers MAY opt-in to `0o640` group-readable for shared-CI cases via explicit `mode=` argument + documented umask interaction (e.g., `umask 0o027` for CI runner) — `0o644` is REJECTED as default for any audit-trail JSONL). **Migration semantic for legacy files** *(Round-7 amendment per T3 round-4 NEEDS-ATTENTION conf=0.91 NEW-CLASS finding on commit `df37fb1`; closes non-migrating gap caught by codex GPT-5.5 BRIDGE-MODE — POSIX `os.open` applies `mode` ONLY when `O_CREAT` actually CREATES the file)*: pre-existing files at `0o644` (created under Round-3-through-5 mandates pre-Round-6) RETAIN their world-readable perms after open, leaving the audit-trail leak intact unless coerced. After every `os.open`, the caller MUST: (i) read `current_mode = stat.S_IMODE(os.fstat(fd).st_mode)`; (ii) if `current_mode != mode` AND the file is owned by caller-uid, call `os.fchmod(fd, mode)` to coerce existing file to the mode invariant; (iii) if `os.fchmod` raises (`PermissionError` due to read-only mount, alien owner, ACL conflict on Windows NTFS, etc.), FAIL CLOSED — propagate the exception rather than proceeding with non-conforming perms (the audit-trail invariant is enforced everywhere or fails loudly). Document in commit body for any consumer applying this rule: one-time migration shell command `find .claude/state -name '*.jsonl' -perm /044 -exec chmod 0600 {} +` (POSIX) OR `Get-ChildItem -Path .claude/state -Filter *.jsonl -Recurse | Where-Object { ($_ | Get-Acl).AccessToString -match 'Everyone Allow Read' } | ForEach-Object { icacls $_.FullName /inheritance:r /grant ${env:USERNAME}:F }` (Windows) for legacy `mcp_health.jsonl` / `subagent_transcripts.jsonl` / `codex_postcommit_reviews.jsonl` / `subagent_start.jsonl` / `worktree_lifecycle_audit.jsonl` files created at `0o644` per pre-Round-6 mandates. The `O_CREAT` flag ensures a missing log auto-creates rather than failing the first writer; **if `os.open` raises (read-only mount, permission denied, disk full), the exception MUST propagate — do not catch-and-ignore** (per Round-5 F-1 silent-failure finding). Take an **exclusive advisory lock** (`fcntl.flock(fd, LOCK_EX)` on POSIX / `msvcrt.locking` on Windows); **if neither primitive is available, or if the platform does not enforce advisory locks (e.g., NFS without NLM support), FAIL CLOSED — raise rather than proceeding without a lock** (per Round-5 F-2 NFS-silent-succeed finding). **Windows separate-lockfile mechanism** *(Round-7c per T3 round-7b NEEDS-ATTENTION conf=0.78 NEW-CLASS finding on commit `48c49fb` caught by codex GPT-5.5 BRIDGE-MODE)*: `msvcrt.locking` locks `nbytes` from CURRENT file-pointer position, NOT the whole file like POSIX `fcntl.flock`. Under O_APPEND the JSONL fd's pointer moves on each write, breaking lock-release symmetry (LK_UNLCK at the new pointer would find no lock at the byte LK_LOCK was issued for). Round-7b workaround (shipped at `scripts/_atomic_jsonl_append.py:_acquire_lock(fd, path)` commit `48c49fb`): open separate `<jsonl-path>.lock` file with 1-byte placeholder + lock byte 0 of the LOCKFILE (no writes to lockfile means file pointer stays at byte 0). Module returns `lock_fd` for Windows callers to release; `None` for POSIX. **Lock-protocol rollout constraint** *(Round-7c per same T3 finding)*: when the lock protocol bumps (direct-jsonl-fd → separate-lockfile-v1, or separate-lockfile-v1 → separate-lockfile-v2-versioned), enforce single-version deployment for the entire concurrent-writer cohort. Old + new code locking DIFFERENT lock domains do NOT mutually exclude — concurrent writers can race even though each ALONE acquires its lock correctly. Mitigations (pick ONE before any concurrent rollout): **(i) transitional dual-lock**: acquire both old AND new protocol locks in series during the transition window; **(ii) runtime version-marker**: write protocol-version byte to lockfile + fail-closed on read-version-mismatch (FORWARD-REF for v2 lock protocol bump); **(iii) single-version cohort barrier**: coordinate cohort upgrade via deployment system before any new-version runs. Currently sss has ZERO consumers of `_atomic_jsonl_append.py` (FORWARD-REF wire-up Ships 2-5 pending per `tmp/wave22-orchestrator-salvage-jsonl-mode-bits-audit-2026-05-05.md`), so the version-skew window is THEORETICAL until first hook migrates to use the module. Future protocol bumps MUST honor one of (i)/(ii)/(iii). HOLD the lock across BOTH (a) JSON-encoding the record AND (b) the single low-level `os.write(fd, encoded_bytes)` — never use buffered text writes (`f.write(json.dumps(rec) + "\n")` via Python file objects can split into multiple writes). **If JSON encoding raises (`UnicodeEncodeError`, non-serializable type), release the lock and propagate the exception — do not silently drop the record** (per Round-5 F-3 silent-record-drop finding). For records where **`len(encoded_bytes)` — the byte count AFTER JSON encoding, NOT the key count of the dict —** exceeds the platform atomic-write bound (≤PIPE_BUF 4KB POSIX; ≤512 bytes for Windows or treat the lock as the sole correctness boundary), reject the record OR shard via option (b) filename-namespace; do NOT silently truncate (per Round-5 F-5 measurement-target finding). After the write, `os.fsync(fd)` if durability is part of the contract (audit-trail JSONL needs fsync; ephemeral telemetry may skip); **if `os.fsync` raises (`EIO`, `ENOSPC`), propagate the exception — do not silently ignore a durability failure when durability is contracted** (per Round-5 F-4 fsync-failure finding). Use for SHARED JSONL log targets (`mcp_health.jsonl`, `subagent_transcripts.jsonl`, `codex_postcommit_reviews.jsonl` class) where consumers expect interleaved appends from multiple writers and unified-view semantics are required.

### agent_id is attribution-only, NOT collision prevention

Two parallel sessions with different `agent_id` values STILL race on the same shared state path under `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=Z:/claude-sota-installed/.claude` env-pinning per §Anti-patterns above. The `agent_id` field disambiguates JSONL records POST-hoc (which agent wrote which entry); it does NOT prevent two writers from racing on the same file path. Collision prevention REQUIRES the boundary in step 2 of §The mandate above.

### Main-session failure mode (no agent_id)

When the hook fires from the main session (no agent context), `agent_id` is None / absent. Step 1 persists `null` (attribution placeholder) but step 2's collision boundary MUST still apply — main-session-vs-main-session race is the SAME class as agent-vs-agent race when two parallel `claude` sessions run concurrently against the shared `Z:/claude-sota-installed/.claude/` config dir.

Filename-namespace with `<process_id>` works for ALL three race classes (main-vs-main, agent-vs-agent, main-vs-agent); agent_id-only namespace works only for agent-vs-agent and FAILS for main-vs-main. When choosing namespace shape, prefer `<process_id>` (universal) over `<agent_id8>` (agent-only) unless the hook is structurally restricted to agent context.

Operator discipline (named-topic uniqueness) per §Anti-patterns "Topic-named verdict file write-collision" COMPLEMENTS but does NOT replace the mechanical boundary above. Defense-in-depth: mechanical boundary (mandatory) + operator discipline (advisory).

### Mandatory-guard promotion (FORWARD-REF → enforceable)

Per `port-note-discipline.md §3 Discipline 2` FORWARD-REF retirement: one previously-FORWARD-REF guard ELEVATES to enforceable mandate this round-2 fix-forward. The chosen guard: `_atomic_jsonl_append.py` shared module that wraps every JSONL append with the boundary in step 2 of §The mandate above (atomic temp-rename + `os.replace` for full-file writes; `O_APPEND` POSIX line-atomicity ≤ PIPE_BUF guarantee for JSONL appends; `O_EXCL` for first-write no-clobber).

Status: PARTIAL-ACTIVE since 2026-05-05 (Wave 31 fire-34 Mia n=35+n=36 disposition correction). Module shipped at `scripts/_atomic_jsonl_append.py` with first consumer `.claude/hooks/scripts/eval_case_compliance_observer.py` (Ship 2a R5 commit `a16fbe1`); concrete-verification per `closed-loop-recursive-narrowing.md §Outcome A monotone-decline path` shipped at commit `e2bc039` (Ship 2a-test "3 fail-closed regression tests close severity-gate concrete-verification gap"). T2 mechanical-enforcement remains FORWARD-REF — `codex_t2_pre_commit_gate.py` exists at `.claude/hooks/scripts/` but does NOT yet wrap-check JSONL-emitting hooks (Grep `_atomic_jsonl_append` in `codex_t2_pre_commit_gate.py` returns no hits 2026-05-05 per Mia probe Wave 31 fire-34). Operator-discipline mandate active per §Mandatory mechanical collision-guard mechanism table; FULL-ACTIVE pending T2 wrapper-check ship; commits adding new JSONL-emitting hooks without `_atomic_jsonl_append` wrapper currently rely on operator review per `layered-gates-architecture.md §5 Layer 2 commit-gate enforcer` semantics. Per `port-note-discipline.md §3 Discipline 2 FORWARD-REF retirement`: partial retirement applied (module-and-consumer status retired; mechanical-enforcement status preserved as FORWARD-REF until T2 wrapper-check ships).

## Anti-patterns

- **Two `claude` sessions in two terminal tabs without `--worktree`** — the documented 2026-04-27 race instance.
- **Manually creating worktrees outside `.claude/worktrees/` and forgetting to add to .gitignore** — leaks temp branches into commits. The sss harness gitignores `.claude/worktrees/` per commit `d57ddf5`.
- **Disabling agent-level isolation by removing `isolation: worktree` from agent frontmatter** — restores the inner-layer race the agent system was designed to prevent.
- **Topic-named verdict file write-collision (operator-discipline anti-pattern)** — `.claude/state/codex_consult_<topic>_OUT.txt` files write-collide if two parallel worktrees fire T1 on the same topic; second writer wins, silently overwriting the first. Mitigation: operator discipline (don't fire concurrent T1 on identical topic). SHA-prefixed `codex_review_HEAD_<sha8>.txt` files cannot collide (commit content differs ⇒ sha8 differs). Append-only JSONL is collision-tolerant per OS append semantics. Wave 18 architect audit (`tmp/wave18-architect-parallel-session-audit-2026-05-04.md` Surface 3+7+8) refuted the prior "each worktree should resolve `.claude/state/` relative to its own root" mitigation: under `tools/eee.ps1:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` symbol-anchor `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=Z:/claude-sota-installed/.claude` env-pinning, all worktrees converge to shared parent state via 4 hardcoded `Path("Z:/claude-sota-installed")` sites (`utils.py:50`, `_guard_base.py:63`, `shellcheck_guard.py:62`, `teammate_idle_gate.py:84`) PLUS Pattern B `parents[3]` resolution at `codex_t1_consult_gate.py:212`. Shared-state-by-design IS correct under CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR semantics — it enables single-grep MEMORY.md / verdict-trail / audit-JSONL aggregation. Operator discipline (named-topic uniqueness) replaces aspirational per-worktree state.

## The contract (cardinal rule)

For every Edit / Write / MultiEdit on a design surface (gate is default-in-scope and skips only `_UNIVERSAL_EXCLUSIONS` per `.claude/hooks/scripts/codex_t1_consult_gate.py:23-28,104-108,232,1717-1719`; common in-scope: rules, agents, commands, skills, settings, `.claude/schemas/*.json`, CLAUDE*.md, .mcp.json, PINS.json — NOT exhaustive):

1. **Opus drafts**. Synthesize from primary sources (Z:/repos/deps file:line, official docs, prior in-repo rules). Write the consult prompt that frames the design.
2. **Codex audits at T1**. Fire `codex exec --ephemeral -p deep-review-exec --output-last-message .claude/state/codex_consult_<topic>_OUT.txt < .claude/state/codex_consult_<topic>.txt` BEFORE writing the design surface (or at minimum, in parallel — but with the file unstaged until verdict integrates). **Canonical pair-basename rule**: prompt path is `.claude/state/codex_consult_<topic>.txt`; verdict path is `.claude/state/codex_consult_<topic>_OUT.txt`. The codex_t1_consult_gate `_consult_pairs()` algorithm strips `_OUT` from output basename and looks for prompt at exact stem — `codex_consult_<topic>_PROMPT.txt` does NOT pair with `codex_consult_<topic>_OUT.txt`. Operator-side fix for FM-08 codex-t1-gate WARN false-positive class (n=14+ session arc 2026-04-29→05-02 caused by my prompts living in `tmp/` instead of `.claude/state/<topic>.txt`).
3. **Verdict integrates**. Apply first-round dispositions from `cmc-verdict-shapes.md §Verdict shapes + closed-loop integration`: APPROVE → ship; NEEDS-REVISION → apply prescribed edits as Pattern A fix-forward per `.claude/rules/codex-t1-fix-forward-pattern.md` (max 1 fix-forward iter per round) and re-fire T1 on the patched design surface; REJECT → STOP, report, and do not commit (remove untracked file before commit).
4. **Verdict reading: EOF FIRST**. Per `feedback_codex_t1_verdict_reading_discipline.md` (TIER-3 local provenance) — codex deep-review-exec may echo verdict templates near the start and emit the real verdict at EOF; `wc -l <file>` first; `grep -nE "VERDICT:|^F-[0-9]|conf=|confidence|APPROVE|NEEDS-REVISION|REJECT|severity (P[0-3])" <file> | tail -20`; then `tail -200 <file>` to confirm the final verdict block at EOF.
5. **Codex audits at T2/T3 (when wired)**. T2 reviews the working tree before commit; T3 fires automatically post-commit.
6. **Ship lands** with the codex verdict file referenced in commit body (`.claude/state/codex_consult_*_OUT.txt` for T1; `.claude/state/codex_review_HEAD_<sha>.txt` for T3 when wired).

The contract is non-negotiable. Recovery paths by violation timing:

- **Pre-commit T1 miss** (file untracked, no commit yet — e.g. v0.1 of this rule): retroactive T1 + single fix-forward if verdict permits. NEEDS-REVISION → fix-forward; APPROVE → ship; REJECT → STOP and remove the file before any commit.
- **Post-commit single-model design surface** (commit landed without T1 verdict on file): per `closed-loop-recursive-narrowing.md §Disposition signal severity gate` — Outcome B REVERT-AND-REMOVE on unresolved high/critical, Outcome C MANUAL-OVERRIDE on medium-with-strong-mitigation.

The first path (pre-commit miss) is the recovery path used by this very rule: v0.1 was untracked when the dogfood failure surfaced, retroactive T1 ran, NEEDS-REVISION verdict integrates here in v0.2 — no commit ever landed without T1 verdict on file.

**Discipline-side / hook-side relationship**: PreToolUse `.claude/hooks/scripts/codex_t1_consult_gate.py:232,1717-1719` targets Edit/Write/MultiEdit; when T1 is absent, the default path warns (non-blocking), while `CODEX_T1_GATE_STRICT=1` with auto-spawn enabled routes through AUTO-T1 at `.claude/hooks/scripts/codex_t1_consult_gate.py:1847-1868` and `_auto_spawn_codex_t1` at `.claude/hooks/scripts/codex_t1_consult_gate.py:1238-1455`. This `§The contract` body is the DISCIPLINE-side complement to hook-side enforcement — agent body sections point HERE rather than duplicate mechanics.

## Profile selection rule

Codex profile presets live at `Z:/claude-sota-installed/.codex/config.toml` (the local repo-resident `.codex/` is the authoritative config; the parent cache path is TIER-3 operational provenance only). Three canonical profiles cover the T1-T7 lifecycle:

- **`deep-review-exec`**: cloud `gpt-5.5` xhigh-effort + danger-full-access sandbox + service_tier=fast + verbosity=high. Used by T1 pre-edit consult hook, T3 postcommit hook, T4 post-push hook, and T6 stop-gate. Token budget ~5K-10K per invocation.
- **`deep-review`**: cloud `gpt-5.5` xhigh-effort + read-only sandbox + service_tier=fast + verbosity=high. Used by T5 manual `/plan-codex-review` slash command (read-only suffices for prompt-context bounded reads). Token budget ~5K-10K per invocation.
- **`t2-exec`** (added iter-93 2026-05-02): cloud `gpt-5.5` HIGH-effort + read-only sandbox + service_tier=fast + verbosity=medium. Used for **operator-side custom-prompt T2 reviews** ONLY: `codex exec --ephemeral -p t2-exec < .claude/state/codex_t2_<topic>.txt > .claude/state/codex_t2_<topic>_OUT.txt 2>&1`. Token budget ~1K-3K per invocation.

**Important asymmetry — T2 commit-time runtime hook does NOT use `-p`**: the runtime pre-commit gate `codex_t2_pre_commit_gate.py:424` uses `codex exec review --uncommitted` which REJECTS `-p` per `codex-cli-flag-positioning.md` matrix row 1. The hook routes via codex CLI's default profile. The `t2-exec` profile is exclusively for operator-side standalone T2 fires with custom prompts.

**Legacy / non-T1-T7 profiles**:
- **`headless-exec`** (gemma4:vision local Ollama): RETIRED for operator-side T2 custom-prompt reviews per n=2 same-arc 180s timeouts. Still correct for pure classification / image / multimodal tasks.
- **`local`** / **`review`** / **`strict`**: see `.codex/config.toml:[profiles.X]` blocks.

Pick by surface complexity and depth-of-reasoning needed, not by file count.

## Timeout + failover policy

- T1 pre-edit consult: **240s narrow** (3-axis prompt) / **900s deep** (full design audit). Narrow is default; escalate to deep only when the design touches multiple sibling rules or introduces a new cite-class.
- T2/T3/T4: **120-180s** sufficient for `--uncommitted` or postcommit-diff scope.
- T5 plan-stage: **240s**.
- T6 stop-gate: **900s** (covers full session-end review).

**On timeout**: fail-closed → mine the partial trace for embedded evidence, document the timeout in the commit body (`T1 INCONCLUSIVE-TIMEOUT after 240s — partial trace mined, no NEW-CLASS findings emerged`), proceed only if no high-severity findings surfaced from the partial output. `feedback_codex_t1_timeout_extract_partial_evidence.md` is TIER-3 local pattern provenance.

### On codex unavailable

(`codex exec` returns cmd-not-found / 3 consecutive failures): the documented `local-judge` MCP fallback is currently UNAVAILABLE — `local-judge` is in `.claude/settings.json:disabledMcpjsonServers` as of 2026-05-03. Recovery options:

- **(a) DEFAULT — Queue + retry**: queue T1 unavailable + codex re-review when codex CLI recovers (preserves cross-model consensus invariant). **Maximum queue window**: 4h for medium-risk ships; 24h for low-risk ships. If beyond window: high-risk BLOCK; medium-risk evaluate (b) with `[OVERRIDE]` marker; low-risk proceed with Pattern B HNF per `closed-loop-recursive-narrowing.md`.
- **(b) FALLBACK — Direct Ollama HTTP bridge** at `http://127.0.0.1:11700/api/generate` against `qwen3.6:judge` model. Backend liveness MEASURED [VERIFIED 2026-05-03 via curl `/api/version` returning `{"version":"0.22.1"}` + `/api/tags` listing `qwen3.6:judge` + `gemma4:vision`].

> **⚠️ CAUTION — Option (b) UNCERTIFIED.** Neither the `/api/generate` endpoint nor the `qwen3.6:judge` model's verdict-shape compatibility has been smoke-tested for cross-model T1 verdict-composition. **First-use of option (b) MUST probe before trusting verdicts**: send a minimal payload with `"stream": false` explicitly (without it, Ollama `/api/generate` defaults to NDJSON streaming and JSON-shape parse will false-negative) + verify `{"response": "..."}` JSON shape returns within 60s + verify model emits APPROVE / NEEDS-REVISION / REJECT structured output as expected by `cmc-verdict-shapes.md §Verdict shapes`. If smoke-probe fails, fall back to option (a) deferred-queue rather than trust an uncertified verdict.

Mark commit body — option (a): `T1 via option-a-deferred — codex re-review queued`; option (b) **DOWNGRADED-MODE**: `T1 DOWNGRADED: qwen3.6:judge via Ollama (UNCERTIFIED — cross-model gate NOT satisfied; GPT-5.5 unavailable); ship under Outcome C MANUAL-OVERRIDE per closed-loop-recursive-narrowing.md with explicit [OVERRIDE] marker; codex re-review queued when GPT-5.5 available`. # TIER-3 local codification provenance only: this rule was promoted from `synthesis-layer-verify.md §Pre-apply Mia rule on agent ship-prescriptions` sub-section (Wave 14 codification commit `10d9455` 2026-05-04) to standalone rule after n=8 cumulative dogfood.

When an agent (architect / codex T1 prescription / sota-researcher / Explore / general-purpose / codex-rescue / gpt5-reviewer) returns a ship-prescription with `prescribed_edits` / specific file:line claims about gaps to close, **pre-apply the Mia rule (verify against runtime state) BEFORE writing any Edit**. The agent's prescription IS NOT TRUSTED until verified — even when conf ≥ 0.90 + Pattern A trigger.

The pattern: **AGENT reads brief context but DOES NOT probe runtime state → produces CATEGORY-CLAIM that LOOKS LIKE OPERATIONAL-CLAIM** (per `synthesis-layer-verify.md §Subclaim-type discriminator`). Agents systematically conflate "should be wired" with "is wired", "should be 80" with "is 80", "is unwired" with "is wired", without checking actual state via `git log` / `Grep` / `Glob`. This rule converts post-hoc OVER detection (existing `synthesis-layer-verify.md §Reporting categories` shape) into PRE-emptive verification (this rule's shape) BEFORE any Edit fires.

## When this rule applies

Trigger on **prescription shape, regardless of file class**. Apply to actionable prescription shapes:

- `prescribed_edits` listing specific file:line + content gaps
- gap-claim ("X is unwired" / "X is missing" / "X needs adding")
- quantitative claim ("70→80" / "12 files" / "5 hooks")
- status flip ("X is FORWARD-REF; promote to ACTIVE")

Do **NOT** apply to (avoid paying the discipline tax on non-actionable returns):

- Pure analysis returns (no `prescribed_edits` / no concrete file:line claim)
- Pure HONEST-NON-FINDING returns (agent already probed and found nothing)
- Pure read-only review output (gpt5-reviewer audit summary without specific edits)

## How to apply (BEFORE writing any Edit)

For each prescription:

1. **Decompose the gap-claim** into testable sub-claims (per `synthesis-layer-verify.md §Within-cycle revision discipline (axis-9)`)
2. **Pick the cheapest probe per sub-claim** (the §Subclaim-type discriminator informs probe-type selection):
   - File-existence claim → `Glob` or `ls -la`
   - Line-content claim → `Read <path>:<lines>` or `Grep`
   - Wire-status claim → `Grep <hook-name> .claude/settings.json`
   - Closed-loop arc claim → `git log --grep="<surface>" --oneline`
   - Count claim → actual `wc -l` / `Grep -c` not memory
   - SHAPE-CLAIM (settings.json hook entry / .mcp.json server / hook JSONL payload) → `Grep` + schema-validate per `synthesis-layer-verify.md §Output-form verification modifier`
3. **Verify EACH sub-claim**. If ≥1 sub-claim refuted → CATEGORY-CLAIM drift detected
4. **Classify a refuted gap-prescription as OVER and drop it.** Reserve HONEST-NON-FINDING for an agent/operator report that explicitly probed an assumed target and found no such target (per `synthesis-layer-verify.md §Reporting categories` OVER vs HNF distinction). Do NOT silently apply the prescription; document the refutation in commit body
5. **Apply only the verified-surviving prescriptions** in the single atomic Pattern A fix-forward commit per `.claude/rules/codex-t1-fix-forward-pattern.md §Pattern A` — this rule is an admissibility filter BEFORE Pattern A's atomic-apply step (first drop OVER prescriptions, then apply all surviving verified prescriptions atomically)

## Alternate-install-path probe discipline (Wave 112 Ship 2CC archeology codification — n=36)

**Trigger**: any prescription class proposing CLI install (`npm install -g <pkg>`, `cargo install <crate>`, `pip install <pkg>`, `go install <module>`, `gh release download`, `winget install`, `uv tool install`, `pipx install`, etc).

**Anti-pattern caught at Wave 112 Ship 2CC archeology** (n=29→36 ladder advance, 5 OVER catches in single ship): original Ship A1 Mia probe used `command -v <cli>` only — checks PATH-availability but MISSES alternate install paths. Effective state: 5 of 5 "GENUINE-GAP" CLIs were ALREADY INSTALLED in alternate paths SHADOWED by Ship A1's installs:
- typos: Wave 62 `.local/bin/typos` v1.46.0 (PATH-resolved) shadowed Ship A1 `.cargo/bin/typos.exe` v1.46.1
- osv-scanner: Wave 62 `.local/bin/osv-scanner` v2.3.6 shadowed Ship A1 `~/go/bin/osv-scanner.exe` v2.3.8
- semgrep: Wave 62 `.local/bin/semgrep` v1.162.0 (uv tool idempotent — no shadow created)
- ast-grep: npm-global `@ast-grep/cli@0.42.0` shadowed Ship A1 `.cargo/bin/ast-grep.exe`
- lefthook: WinGet `evilmartians.lefthook` shadowed Ship A1 npm-global lefthook

**Cost of incomplete probe**: 115 MB shadow installs (Ship A2-RECONCILE recovered) + version-drift confusion + manifest documentation gap (Ship A3 closed) + 3 follow-up ships (2CC + A2-RECONCILE + A3) to operationally close.

**Fortified probe (mandatory for INSTALL-class prescriptions)**:

```bash
# Step 1: PATH probe (BUT not sufficient alone)
command -v <cli>

# Step 2: ALTERNATE install path probe (NEW — required per Wave 112 Ship 2CC codification)
find /z/claude-sota-installed/.local/bin /z/claude-sota-installed/.cargo/bin ~/go/bin ~/.local/bin /c/Users/*/AppData/Roaming/npm /c/Users/*/AppData/Local/Microsoft/WinGet/Links -maxdepth 1 -name '<cli>*' -type f 2>/dev/null

# Step 3: Channel-registry probes (per platform)
npm ls -g 2>/dev/null | grep -i <cli>           # npm-global registry
uv tool list 2>/dev/null | grep -i <cli>        # uv tool registry
pipx list 2>/dev/null | grep -i <cli>           # pipx registry
winget list <cli> 2>/dev/null                   # WinGet registry (Windows)
brew list 2>/dev/null | grep -i <cli>           # Homebrew (macOS/Linux)

# Step 4: ALL hits = pre-existing canonical install if any returned non-empty
# If pre-existing exists → DROP install prescription per OVER classification
# Document canonical channel in manifest if not yet cited
```

**Probe-yield discipline**: per `synthesis-layer-verify.md §Subclaim-type discriminator` — INSTALL-class is OPERATIONAL-CLAIM; cheap multi-channel probe is mandatory cost-floor (~3-5s for full enumeration vs ~5-15min revert + uninstall + manifest cleanup if shadow installed).

**When to apply**: any agent prescription containing `<install-command> <package>` where install-command ∈ {npm install -g, cargo install, pip install, go install, gh release download, winget install, uv tool install, pipx install, brew install}. The probe-shape MUST enumerate ALL relevant alternate paths for the package's canonical channel + competing channels per platform.

## Empirical evidence ladder (n=36 cumulative — n=8 same-arc-codification-basis + n=21 cross-arc post-codification + n=7 Wave 112 Ship A1+2CC archeology shadow-install class)

## Why this works

Agents are calibrated to find gaps; they're NOT calibrated to verify "is the gap still open?" before prescribing. Their reasoning surface is BRIEF + LOCAL-CONTEXT-WINDOW, not REPO-RUNTIME-STATE. The Mia-rule pre-apply discipline closes this gap by inserting a cheap (~1-3s) runtime probe between prescription-receipt and Edit-application.

ROI math: `Glob`/`Grep` probe ≈ 1-3s; reverting a wrong Edit ≈ 5-15min (revert + verify + arc memory). Cheap probe pays for itself ~100× per refuted prescription. At n=3/session base rate this session, savings = ~15-45min/session × N sessions/mo = compounding.

The rule is **bidirectional** — saves false-OVER ship cycles (rows 4, 6, 7) AND validates true-positive gap-claims (rows 5, 8). Pattern A admissibility filter shape: drop OVER, apply VERIFIED-GENUINE atomically.

## Anti-patterns

- **Trust agent prescription verbatim because conf ≥ 0.90** — refuted by n=3 same-arc evidence + n=5 cross-arc evidence. Codex T1 verdict at conf=0.92 still produced an OVER on Wave 13 prescription #2; architect at no-conf-stated produced 2 OVERs (Wave 12 S1 + S3); Wave 8 sota-researcher at no-conf-stated produced staleness drift on Ship #1 spec. Confidence does NOT correlate with prescription-truth on already-closed surfaces.
- **Skip cheap probe ("just N seconds")** — refuted by ROI math above (1-3s probe vs 5-15min revert; ~100× ROI per catch).
- **Cite the agent's verdict file as authority for the prescription** — per `cross-model-consensus.md §Source-cite discipline for consult prompts`: agent verdicts (`.claude/state/codex_consult_*_OUT.txt` + agent inline returns) are TIER-3 evidence trails, NOT TIER-1 sources. For local operational claims, the checked file/log/git history is the controlling operational evidence; the agent's prescription is a hypothesis pending probe-confirmation, not a verified fact.
- **Apply prescriptions in single atomic batch without per-prescription verification** — refuted by Wave 13 same-arc evidence: codex T1 prescription #2 was OVER in a 6-prescription batch; if I'd applied all 6 at once, the duplicate would have shipped. Per-prescription verification is necessary even when the agent batches.
- **Conflate OVER with HONEST-NON-FINDING** — these are distinct `synthesis-layer-verify.md §Reporting categories`: OVER = report claims more than git shows (refuted prescription class); HNF = report says "I probed for X, found nothing" (agent did the probe). A refuted gap-prescription where I probed and found the gap closed = OVER, NOT HNF (the agent didn't probe; I did).
- **Apply Mia BEFORE codex T1 finishes** — Mia is a PRE-Edit gate; if codex T1 is still running, wait for verdict (Pattern A) OR honor Pattern B HNF disposition (timeout-without-verdict). DO NOT race Mia probe + Pattern A apply against an in-flight T1 — the T1 may correct or refute the Mia prescription itself (recursive: codex T1 ratifies Mia ratifies prescription).

- **PATH-only probe for INSTALL-class prescriptions** — refuted by Wave 112 Ship A1+2CC archeology n=29→36 (5 OVER catches in single ship). `command -v <cli>` only checks PATH-availability — MISSES alternate install paths (`.local/bin/`, `.cargo/bin/`, `~/go/bin/`, npm-global, WinGet, uv tool dirs). Cost: 115 MB shadow installs + 3 follow-up ships to operationally close. Use the fortified multi-channel probe per §Alternate-install-path probe discipline above.
